species.name: Butterflyfish
mustRead: near-circular plate-thin disc body
dark bar masking the eye
pointed tweezer snout

species.name: Angelfish
mustRead: tall disc body as deep as it is long
trailing dorsal and anal fin filaments
small mouth and a spine on the gill cover
species.note: marine angelfish (Pomacanthidae), not the freshwater triangular one

species.name: Surgeonfish
mustRead: scalpel-like spine at the base of the tail
oval compressed body with a steep forehead
long low dorsal fin running the whole back

species.name: Tang
mustRead: round plate-like body with a sharp tail-base spine
small pointed grazing snout
crescent tail
species.note: same family as surgeonfish - drawn as a blue or yellow tang

species.name: Triggerfish
mustRead: eyes set far back and high, well away from the mouth
erectile trigger spine on the forehead
rowing second dorsal and anal fins on a leathery diamond body

species.name: Parrotfish
mustRead: fused beak-like teeth plates
blunt bulging forehead
large paddle pectoral fins used for rowing

species.name: Wrasse
mustRead: protruding buck teeth on a pointed snout
cigar-shaped body
large fan pectoral fins doing the swimming

species.name: Cardinalfish
mustRead: oversized eyes for the head
two clearly separate dorsal fins
large mouth on a short deep body

species.name: Lionfish
mustRead: fan of long venomous dorsal spines
feathery separated pectoral fin rays spread like wings
red-brown and white zebra banding

species.name: Pufferfish
mustRead: round inflated balloon body
big protruding eyes and a small beaked mouth
tiny fluttering fins with no pelvic fins
species.note: usually drawn inflated; uninflated it is a normal ovoid fish about twice as long as deep

species.name: Boxfish
mustRead: rigid armoured box-shaped carapace
tiny fins and tail poking out of the box
big eyes and pursed lips at the front

species.name: Seahorse
mustRead: horse-like head held at right angles to the body
curled prehensile tail with no tail fin
ringed bony armour plating
species.note: much taller than wide - the only fin of note is the small fluttering dorsal on the back

species.name: Moray Eel
mustRead: gaping mouth of needle teeth held permanently open
single fin ridge running the whole length of the back
no pectoral fins and no gill covers, just a round gill pore

species.name: Pipefish
mustRead: needle-thin ringed body
tiny tube snout with a pinhole mouth
seahorse head held in line with the body

species.name: Rabbitfish
mustRead: small blunt rabbit-like snout with a tiny mouth
oval compressed body
row of venomous spines along the dorsal fin

species.name: Sea Bass
mustRead: spiny first dorsal fin ahead of a soft second one
large mouth on a robust perch body
squared or slightly forked tail

species.name: Gray Whale
mustRead: row of knuckle bumps along the back instead of a dorsal fin
mottled grey skin crusted with barnacles and lice patches
narrow arched rostrum with a slightly bowed jawline

species.name: Tuna
mustRead: stiff crescent-moon tail on a narrow keeled stalk
row of small yellow finlets to the tail
fat torpedo body with fins folding into grooves

species.name: Haddock
mustRead: dark thumbprint blotch above the pectoral fin
black lateral line
tall pointed first dorsal fin and three dorsals in all

species.name: Pollock
mustRead: three dorsal fins and two anal fins
protruding lower jaw
pale lateral line on an olive-green back

species.name: Sperm Whale
mustRead: enormous square blunt head taking up a third of the body
narrow underslung toothed lower jaw
knuckled dorsal hump instead of a fin, and a single blowhole at the front-left of the head

species.name: Pilot Whale
mustRead: bulbous melon forehead overhanging the mouth
long low swept-back dorsal fin set well forward on the back
black body with a pale anchor patch on the throat

species.name: Beaked Whale
mustRead: long dolphin-like beak on a bulging melon
small dorsal fin set far back
pair of tusk teeth erupting from the lower jaw of males, body scarred with rake marks

species.name: Great White Shark
mustRead: conical snout over a mouth of triangular serrated teeth
sharp line where the grey back meets the white belly
tall triangular dorsal fin and a broad crescent tail
